title: A woman clothed with the sun (Apocalypse 12)
word: A woman clothed with the sun
hook: the moon under her feet and twelve stars; read on the Assumption as Mary and the Church

segments.voice: Yesterday, a great multitude, from every nation, in white, with palms. Your line was every tongue. Whose language did you picture in that crowd? Day six hundred twenty-seven.

Nearly six hundred years before Christ, Babylon's army burned the temple in Jerusalem. After that, the ark of the covenant, the gold-covered chest that held the tablets of the law, is never seen again in the Bible's history. Nobody knows what became of it. One old story, in Second Maccabees, says the prophet Jeremiah hid it in a cave on a mountain until God gathers his people again. Then, at the very end of Apocalypse eleven, John sees God's temple in heaven open, and there it is: the ark. And the very next thing he sees isn't a chest at all. It's a woman.
screen: `THE ARK, LOST WITH THE TEMPLE.` → `SEEN AGAIN IN HEAVEN.` → `THEN, A WOMAN.`

segments.voice: Right after the ark, in the Douay-Rheims: "A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars." She is about to give birth, crying out in pain. And a second sign appears: a great red dragon, with seven heads and ten horns, standing in front of her, waiting to devour the child as soon as it's born. The child is born, a son who will rule all the nations, and he's caught up to God and to his throne. The woman flees into the wilderness, to a place God has prepared for her. Then war breaks out in heaven, Michael and his angels against the dragon, and the dragon is thrown down. The text names him: that old serpent, the devil. That old serpent takes us all the way back to Genesis, where God tells the serpent there will be enmity between him and the woman, between his seed and hers. Who is the woman? Catholic tradition doesn't pick just one answer. She is Mary, who bore the child who rules the nations; the Church reads this passage on the feast of the Assumption, in August. She is also the Church, the people of God, who bring Christ into the world in pain and are kept safe in the wilderness. And many readers also see Israel in her twelve stars, the twelve tribes. The symbols carry more than one meaning at once. Notice how the scene began: with the ark of the covenant. Catholic tradition has long called Mary the ark of the new covenant, the one who carried God within her.
screen: `THE ARK SEEN IN HEAVEN.` · `A WOMAN, A CHILD, A DRAGON.` · `THAT OLD SERPENT, FROM GENESIS.` · `MARY, THE CHURCH, AND ISRAEL.` · then, large: `A WOMAN CLOTHED WITH THE SUN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look at the moon, or picture it. If it's evening and the moon is up, go to a window or step outside. If not, close your eyes and picture it, the way you've seen it on a clear night. Breathe. Imagine the moon under someone's feet, as if it were a footstool. Then the sun around her, and twelve stars over her head. Let the size of it land: the whole sky as clothing. Then remember that she was also a mother in pain, with a dragon in front of her, and she was kept safe. If you pray, you can ask Mary to pray for you. If you don't, just stay with the sky. The bell holds the time.
A woman clothed with the sun. Apocalypse twelve: the moon under her feet, twelve stars on her head; Catholics see Mary and the Church in her. Today's word.

segments.voice: Your line: clothed with the sun. Tonight, look for the moon, and if you find it, remember the woman standing on it. Day six hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: Catholics hear Apocalypse 12 on the Solemnity of the Assumption, August 15, and Marian art, especially images of the Immaculate Conception, often shows Mary with the sun, the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars.

notes: 2 Maccabees 2:4–8 (Jeremiah hides the ark in a cave on the mountain) paraphrased and framed as an old story; the ark's disappearance with the Babylonian destruction (587/586 BC) is the usual account, though its exact fate is unknown. Confirm.
Assumption, Mass during the Day: first reading Apocalypse 11:19a; 12:1–6a, 10ab. Confirm.
Mary as Ark of the New Covenant: traditional title (Litany of Loreto: Ark of the Covenant). Confirm.
The woman read as Mary, the Church and Israel: common in Catholic interpretation; not ranked.
